idea-plugin.name: SOPS Editor
idea-plugin.description:
Edit SOPS-encrypted files directly in your JetBrains IDE. The plugin opens a split view with the decrypted content on one side and the raw ciphertext on the other, and re-encrypts the file when you save.

Features

  • Side-by-side decrypted and encrypted view for any SOPS file
  • Automatic re-encryption on Ctrl+S, with an opt-out in settings and a manual save action
  • Decrypted, read-only diffs of SOPS files in Git history and local changes
  • Context menu actions for Encrypt with SOPS, Decrypt with SOPS and New SOPS Encrypted File
  • Default shortcuts Ctrl+Alt+E to encrypt and Ctrl+Alt+D to decrypt
  • Supports .env, YAML, JSON, INI and binary (.sops, .bin) files, matching the sops CLI itself
  • Age key and PGP support through the system sops binary
  • A setup validator that checks your sops binary, age key file and environment
  • A log file with secret masking for AGE keys, PEM private key blocks and SSH public keys

Requirements

  • The sops CLI on your PATH, or a full path configured in settings
  • An age key file (default: ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt) or a configured PGP key
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.2.0

  • Projects stored in WSL now work. On Windows, files on \\wsl.localhost\ or \\wsl$\ paths are handled by sops inside the distribution, so the project's .sops.yaml rules and the age key file in WSL apply.
  • New setting SOPS executable in WSL for the sops command or path used inside WSL.
  • Decrypted diffs: a new diff viewer SOPS: decrypted shows SOPS files in Git history, local changes and Compare with Revision as read-only plaintext, marked with an open lock icon. The All-in-One Diff does not offer it. The ciphertext stays available in Side-by-side viewer. Can be turned off in settings.
  • With automatic re-encryption turned off, Encrypt with SOPS (Ctrl+Alt+E) now saves the open SOPS file.
  • With sops 3.10 or newer, plaintext is passed to sops through stdin, so no plaintext temporary files are written.
  • A failed New SOPS Encrypted File no longer leaves a plaintext file behind.
  • A SOPS file that cannot be written on save, for example because it is read-only, is reported and the changes stay in the editor.
  • A failed save no longer offers a Try Again that decrypted the file again and replaced the unsaved changes.
  • A sops call that hangs is stopped after two minutes, and closing a decrypted diff stops its sops process.
  • Changes typed while a save is running now stay marked as unsaved.
  • Saving again while a save is still running no longer starts a second sops run; the newer text is saved right after the first one, so older ciphertext can no longer overwrite it.
  • An empty file encrypted in binary mode now opens as a binary SOPS file instead of a JSON document.
  • If sops cannot be started, the log no longer contains the path of the sops executable.
  • Updated the build toolchain and pinned the GitHub Actions used for builds and releases.

1.1.1

  • Fixed a bug that could cause high CPU usage while a SOPS file was open: the editor reported the encrypted file to the IDE's code-analysis daemon while showing the decrypted contents, which made the daemon restart in a loop.

1.1.0

  • Binary-mode SOPS files (.sops + .bin) now open in the split-view editor with the JSON envelope shown read-only on the right and the inner extension driving syntax highlighting on the left.
  • SOPS files are auto-detected from their content, so files with non-standard extensions are picked up automatically.
  • TOML dropped from the supported list; .toml SOPS files are detected as binary mode (which is what SOPS actually produces for them).
  • Save no longer crashes with a Write-unsafe context error on newer IntelliJ Platform builds.
  • Added SECURITY.md and a least-privilege permissions block to the build workflow.

1.0.0

First public release. See the README on GitHub for the feature list and setup instructions.
